title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — corruption truly sin; reatus even of infants
pass_a_gloss: PLAC: What? Is corruption not truly sin? Does reatus not follow from it? Does it not make every human—even infants still hidden in the womb—guilty of eternal death before God? Must we not first be justified from it? Strange that those who charge us with novelty depart so openly from the doctrine all Protestants receive.
pass_b_english: PLAC. What? Is corruption not truly sin? Does reatus not follow from it? Does it not make all and each human, not even little ones excepted still hiding in their mothers' womb, guilty of eternal death before God? Must we not first of all be justified from it? It is strange that those who accuse us of innovated doctrine depart so openly from the doctrine received by all Protestants.
source_text: PLAC. Quid? Nonne corruptio est vere peccatum? Nonne ex illa consequitur reatus? Nonne omnes & singulos homines, ne parvulis quidem exceptis adhuc in utero matrum delitescentibus, aeternae mortis reos coram Deo peragit? Nonne ab ea nos imprimis justificari oportet? Mirum est qui nos innovatae doctrinae accusant, tam aperte a recepta ab omnibus Protestantibus doctrina discedere.

choices.choice: Corruption truly sin; reatus even of infants; justify from it
